title: CI validation grid and helm value contracts
body:
Context and purpose:
This is a working draft to capture a lightweight, machine-friendly CI validation grid plus an explicit Helm-values contract we can use when wiring Terraform module outputs -> GitOps/Argo deployments in VPC/on-prem environments. Goal: make pre-promote validation, canary gating, and rollback deterministic across customers that run with different isolation patterns (VPC peering, private subnets, air-gapped with OCI proxy).

High-level constraints we need to satisfy:
- Minimal network dependencies in the validation stage (offline-friendly tests for air-gapped installs).
- Deterministic artifact provenance checks (cosign/notation + attestation verification step).
- Terraform modules must expose clear semantic versioned interfaces (inputs/outputs) so Argo/helm promos are predictable.
- Rollouts must have observable SLO signals that map to CI gates (latency/99th, error-rate, token-cost smoke).

CI validation grid (matrix):
Rows = artifact stage (bundle built, image pushed, helm chart packaged), Columns = target topology and test classes. Add a quick-pass vs deep-pass column to allow fast feedback vs pre-release validation.

Matrix example (abbreviated):
- artifact-stage: bundle -> topology: vpc (fast-pass) -> tests: signature presence, chart lint, helm template render with minimal values
- artifact-stage: image -> topology: airgapped-with-proxy (deep-pass) -> tests: cosign verify, attestation fetch, local registry push simulation, smoke inference pod start
- artifact-stage: helm -> topology: onprem-non-root (fast-pass) -> tests: helm install --dry-run, values schema validation, CRD presence check

Test categories and minimal criteria (for gating):
- Security provenance: cosign verification must succeed against configured KMS key; attestation (if present) must include build-info and git commit. Gate: fail if missing or signature mismatch.
- Render-time correctness: helm template must render for the set of supported Kubernetes versions and common value overrides. Gate: render error fails.
- Resource sanity: CPU/memory estimates present, no hostPath or cluster-admin binds without explicit override. Gate: lint warnings escalated based on policy.
- Smoke functionality: Pod(s) start, dependencies resolve (DNS to internal services allowed), health endpoint returns 200 within N seconds. Gate: if unhealthy > T1, fail canary (or mark as degraded depending on policy).
- Telemetry hooks: config must include observability.sink and telemetry.token placeholders; validate that values.schema documents optional vs required fields.

Helm values contract (proposal):
The Terraform modules that produce values for private deployments should emit a small, versioned JSON blob (helm_values_contract) that the GitOps pipeline consumes. Fields and expectations:
- clusterTopology: string (vpc | onprem | airgapped)
- registry: string (OCI endpoint or local registry host)
- imagePullSecret: string (ref) OR placeholder token type
- kmsKeyRef: string (ARN or path) optional but required if images are signed with customer KMS
- observability.sink: string (prometheus|datadog|none) -- pipeline ensures a sane default in fast-pass
- helmChartVersion: semver string
- requiredOverrides: list of strings (namespaced path keys that must be present before promote)
- allowedPatchKeys: list of strings (which helm values keys CI is allowed to auto-fill)
Notes: keep the schema flat and conservative; avoid embedding nested objects beyond one level to simplify simple JSON merges in pipelines. Version this blob using a contractVersion key (e.g., 1.0.0).

Terraform module interface guidance (short):
- Modules expose outputs: helm_values_blob (stringified JSON), image_tag, chart_uri, artifact_provenance_url.
- Use a small contract test in unit/TerraformCI that validates the helm_values_blob keys and types. Fail fast in TF plan stage if contract validation fails.
- Do not output secrets; only references/ARNS/placeholders. Secrets must be injected by the GitOps runtime (sealed secrets, vault sync).

Canary and promotion flow (recommended):
1) Build -> sign -> push artifacts to customer-approved registry (or to staging mirror for air-gapped installs).
2) Terraform apply in infra sandbox to produce helm_values_blob.
3) CI renders helm template with the blob (fast-pass). If render OK, create a canary Argo application with scaled-down replicas and traffic shadowing to canary instances.
4) Canary smoke tests run (health, simple inference, token cost spot-check). Metrics reported to CI via push/poller.
5) If canary passes thresholds for 10m, auto-promote to staged channel; otherwise roll back and open an incident ticket with attached logs and artifact metadata.

Rollback and failure modes (examples):
- Signature rotation mismatch: if cosign verification fails on promotion, automatically revert to previous chart version and pin the TF module to previous artifact_tag. Create ticket for key rotation sync.
- Missing required value: fail early in TF plan and notify release owner with the exact missing key path.
- Canary flapping: if metric oscillation occurs, mark as unstable and run a diagnostic workflow that fetches pod logs, recent kernel OOMs, node resource contention, and publishes to the release PR.

Telemetry and CI observability hooks (what CI needs to record):
- artifact_id, image_digest, chart_digest, cosign_key_id, build_git_sha, build_ts
- canary_run_id, canary_metrics (latency_p50/p95/p99, error_rate), smoke_test_logs (url)
- promotion_decision: auto|manual and reason field

Automation components to create (short TODOs):
- pipeline/checks/helm-values-validator (tiny container that validates contract blob)
- pipeline/checks/provenance-verifier (wraps cosign/notation calls and returns normalized pass/fail)
- argo/app-templater that consumes helm_values_blob and creates ephemeral canary apps with defined traffic-splitting annotations
- tf-module tests that run in GH Actions with a mocked provider for airgapped registries

Open questions / design trade-offs:
- How opinionated do we want on the schema of helm values? Customers with highly customized charts may resist a rigid contract. Proposal: make the contract opt-in via a required_overrides list, otherwise pipeline falls back to a conservative defaults layer.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: what are sensible defaults for token-cost checks on canary? need product input.
- Attestation format: do we require a specific predicate (e.g., SLSA-based) or accept multiple formats and map them during verification?

Quick checklist for a single release (runbook sketch):
- [ ] Build artifact and sign (cosign), publish digest
- [ ] Terraform plan/app to generate helm_values_blob
- [ ] Run helm-values-validator and provenance-verifier
- [ ] If fast-pass OK, create canary Argo application
- [ ] Run smoke tests; collect metrics for 10m
- [ ] If pass, promote; record telemetry and close canary_run
- [ ] If fail, revert chart and pin tf module; attach logs and open ticket

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated on minimal schema and automation pieces; looking for feedback on how heavy-handed the contract should be for VPC/on-prem customers.
- Implementation should favor small, composable validation containers (single-responsibility) so air-gapped customers can run only the subset they need.

References and quick links (draft):
- internal:confluence/private-deploy-ci-patterns (placeholder)
- jira:INF-1789 (validation-grid workstream)

-- Aisha (draft, notes to self)
